mark_breakdown.desc: Combine right-hand side using logarithmic product rule

ai_explanation.concept_rule: One-to-one property of logarithms: $\log_b u = \log_b v \iff u = v$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to take the cube root and stating $x = 8$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Solve quadratic and verify both solutions are in the domain

subparts.solution: $\log_2 x = \log_2 12 - \log_2(7 - x) \implies \log_2 x = \log_2\left(\frac{12}{7 - x}\right) \implies x = \frac{12}{7 - x} \implies x(7 - x) = 12 \implies 7x - x^2 = 12 \implies x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0 \implies x = 3 \text{ or } 4$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Combine logarithms using the quotient rule, equate arguments, and check the domain restrictions ($x > 0$ and $7 - x > 0$).
step_by_step: Both satisfy $0 < x < 7$, so both are valid.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Failing to check whether solutions satisfy the domain of the original logarithmic expressions.

mark_breakdown.desc: Combine logarithms and equate argument to $e^0 = 1$

subparts.solution: $\ln(x^2 - 3) - \ln(2x) = 0 \implies \ln\left(\frac{x^2 - 3}{2x}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{x^2 - 3}{2x} = e^0 = 1 \implies x^2 - 3 = 2x \implies x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 3 \text{ or } -1$. But $x = -1$ does not satisfy the original equation, as $\ln(-2)$ is undefined. Therefore, the only solution is $x = 3$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Logarithmic equations require all arguments to be strictly positive: $x^2 - 3 > 0$ and $2x > 0$.
step_by_step: Reject $x = -1$ because $\ln(2(-1)) = \ln(-2)$ is undefined. The solution is $x = 3$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to discard the extraneous solution $x = -1$.

subparts.solution: $\log_3 x + \log_3(x - 2) = 1 \implies \log_3(x(x - 2)) = 1 \implies x(x - 2) = 3 \implies x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 3 \text{ or } -1$. But $x = -1$ does not satisfy the original equation, as $\log_3(-1)$ is undefined. Therefore, the only solution is $x = 3$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The product rule gives $\log_b(u) + \log_b(v) = \log_b(uv)$, and arguments must be positive ($x > 2$).
step_by_step: Check domain: $x > 2$, so $x = -1$ is extraneous. Hence, $x = 3$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including $x = -1$ as a valid solution without checking log domain.
